documented_not_implemented.detail: flock-you / OUI-SPY firmware-dump research: Flock cameras emit wildcard probe requests ~8x/sec from QCA9377/Liteon OUIs with a specific IE skeleton (Qualcomm LOWI scanning). This is the strongest current Flock tell, but it needs monitor-mode frame capture — the dongle path, not managed scans. Queued behind the capture work.
documented_not_implemented.label: Flock wildcard probe-request fingerprint
documented_not_implemented.source: OUI-SPY Vol. 2 (hacking.fubsypoly.com), Swiz Security probe-request write-up

documented_not_implemented.detail: DJI favours the Wi-Fi form of Remote ID; decoding it needs monitor-mode beacon capture on the dongle. Same future path as above.
documented_not_implemented.label: OpenDroneID over Wi-Fi (vendor IE FA:0B:BC / NAN)

note: Passive-detection signatures from public research only. Every entry names its source and an honest confidence tier: a match is a lead graded by tier, never a verdict. Name/SSID patterns are the weakest tier on purpose — a famous field demo of a commercial detector flagged a Bowflex treadmill as a camera (ALPR Maps, 'Signal Reality Check').

signatures.label: Drone Remote ID broadcast (OpenDroneID)
signatures.source: ASTM F3411 Remote ID: BLE service data UUID 0xFFFA, app code 0x0D. Corroborated by GhostESP aerial detection docs, FlipDeFlock v0.88, AryaOS dronecot-ble, Sparrow-WiFi DroneID.

signatures.label: DJI drone link (BLE)
signatures.source: GhostESP aerial detection docs: DJI advertisements carry service UUID 0xFFE0.

signatures.label: Possible drone — DJI OUI
signatures.source: FlipDeFlock v0.88 drone_ouis table (SZ DJI Technology + DJI Baiwang), resolved against the IEEE MA-L registry. Fallback heuristic only — an OUI says who made the radio, not that an aircraft is present. FlipDeFlock deliberately excludes DJI F8:40:68 (Ronin gimbals) and 20:1F:55 (Osmo handhelds); so do we.

signatures.label: Possible drone — Skydio OUI
signatures.source: FlipDeFlock v0.88 drone_ouis (Skydio — the only one of the five US police-drone vendors holding an IEEE block).

signatures.label: Possible drone — public-safety airframe OUI
signatures.source: FlipDeFlock v0.88 drone_ouis: Teal B0:30:C8, AeroVironment 00:1A:F9, Shield AI 14:DD:48, Freefly EC:71:5E, Zipline 74:B8:0F.

signatures.label: Possible drone — drone SSID pattern
signatures.source: DEF CON 34 PHV Remote ID talk signature table (SSID prefix scored 0.30, the weakest drone clue) + GhostESP drone-SSID matching. Anyone can name a network anything.

signatures.label: Watchlist — Flock-style SSID pattern
signatures.source: Flock-You-Android RF surveillance detection doc (SSID patterns ^flock ^falcon ^sparrow ^condor). Treat as a curiosity flag only: ALPR Maps' reality check found no durable Flock radio signature — the cameras' working radio is LTE, and installer interfaces are inconsistent and often disabled after commissioning.

signatures.label: Watchlist — Flock-style BLE name
signatures.source: Flock-You-Android doc (BLE name ^flock) + flock-you project history. The historical Flock BLE beacon has stopped appearing in at least one region (Swiz Security write-up) — absence proves nothing, presence is a weak lead.

signatures.label: Watchlist — Flock-associated modem OUI
signatures.source: Flock-You-Android doc lists these Quectel LTE-modem OUIs for Flock units. Quectel modules ship in countless unrelated devices — weakest entry in this file, kept for completeness.
